item: A refused or failed rebuild of sources leaves the store as found, the derived view included (audit 0.5.0 A-012, routing 11)
refs: PR #1495; audit 0.5.0 A-012; follows PR #1489 and R205
summary: upgrade_sources_to_composite_key dropped keyword_mentions_all first and decided its schema refusals afterwards, so a store holding a column this build does not know was refused with the view gone, and ensure_source_composite_key recreates the view only after a success: the view stayed missing from the refusal until init_db's own ensure_derived_views a few steps later, and for any direct caller (scale_bench, a migration run on its own) for good (reproduced: view present before, 0 after the refusal; the read found init_db restores it, so the exposure is the steps in between and the direct callers). The refusals that the schema alone decides (unknown column, required column without default, with feed_key counted as present because it is added next) and the read of the extra indexes and triggers now run before the pragma and before any statement that changes the store; the one read that must follow the column being added (old_cols, which decides what is copied) stays after it; the DROP VIEW moved inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a failure after it rolls it back with the rest (SQLite DDL is transactional). This is routing 11's two-phase read, and it is also the only part of A-012 that was a defect and not a hardening: the loop heads in this function were already moved out by R205. tests/test_composite_key_leaves_the_store_as_found.py: refusal leaves the view and the legacy state; the statement trace shows no PRAGMA foreign_keys, DROP, ALTER, CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE or BEGIN before a refusal; a failed copy rolls the view back; a successful rebuild still ends with the view; a table lacking only feed_key is not refused. The read's two interrupt findings are fixed here too (both were on main already): an interrupt that kept the ROLLBACK from reaching the driver let the finally commit a half-finished rebuild, because setting isolation_level on Python 3.13 commits an open transaction, so the finally now rolls back through the driver when a transaction is still open; and an interrupt after the COMMIT met began still True, sent a ROLLBACK that SQLite answered with 'no transaction is active', and the OperationalError replaced the interrupt (boot then swallowed it as a refusal), so the rollback now also requires an open transaction. The read that decides what is copied now follows BEGIN IMMEDIATE and is judged again there, so a column another process added before the write lock is refused, not left out of the copy; and an interrupt raised inside SQLAlchemy's own statement execution (which invalidates the connection, closing the driver one) is no longer replaced by a ProgrammingError from asking that connection about its transaction: the cleanup skips a connection that is invalidated, since closing it rolled the transaction back. Eight of the nine tests fail without the change. Not changed: the Alembic revision that calls the function (same signature and returns), the order of the other boot steps.
